literature.use_in_design: Google SVI motivation; unavailable here, so OHLCV proxy is labelled as indirect.

event_label.winner: ret21_lag >= rolling252 q80 OR prior close within 2% of prior 63d high
event_label.loser: ret21_lag <= rolling252 q20 OR prior close within 2% of prior 63d low

outcomes.abn_volume_z: log(volume)_t standardized by lagged 252d mean/std through t-1
outcomes.range_vol_z: (log(high_t/low_t)*100)^2 standardized by lagged 252d mean/std through t-1
outcomes.gap_abs_z: |log(open_t/close_{t-1})*100| standardized by lagged 252d mean/std through t-1
outcomes.rv_z: (log(close_t/close_{t-1})*100)^2 standardized by lagged 252d mean/std through t-1

windows.all_next_sessions: All next trading sessions after the t-1 winner/loser label
windows.monday_post_weekend: Monday sessions, proxying post-weekend attention release

methodology.test: Ticker-level winner-minus-loser mean differences; one-sample t across tickers within each basket; Welch t for retail-minus-control DiD.
methodology.multiple_testing: Holm adjustment across all within-group and DiD tests (24 total tests).

lookahead_controls.winner_loser_labels: ret21_lag uses close.pct_change(21).shift(1); prior high/low uses close.shift(1).rolling(...). Event labels at date t never use close_t.
lookahead_controls.outcome_standardization: Every outcome z-score uses series.shift(1).rolling(...) for mean/std, so t's outcome is not included in its own benchmark.
lookahead_controls.no_training_split: This is an event-study diagnostic, not an OOS forecast. There is no model selection on the test window; all thresholds are fixed ex ante.

primary_summary.interpretation: Retail-minus-control asymmetry survives Holm correction, but the retail basket's own winner-minus-loser effects do not. This is compatible with retail winner-side attention, but the evidence is relative and exploratory, not an absolute positive winner-side pass.

limitations: No brokerage-login, Google Trends, Reddit, or Stocktwits attention data were used.
Earnings-window attention is not tested; reliable point-in-time earnings dates were outside the free-data scope.
Daily OHLCV cannot separate market-close attention from intraday order flow.
Ticker-level t-tests reduce but do not eliminate common-date cross-sectional dependence.
This is a proxy mechanism screen and should not be treated as causal identification.
